newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel to propose FILP reforms in July.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel to propose FILP reforms in July.

text.p: A government advisory panel will submit interim proposals in July to reform Japan's massive fiscal investment and loans programme (FILP) and FILP-funded semi-governmental bodies, Finance Ministry officials said on Wednesday.
The panel will draft its final reform proposals by the end of this year, when the government finalises its 1998/99 state budget and FILP programme, they said.

The proposals will be submitted to the Finance Ministry, which oversees FILP, and to the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (MPT), which oversees the postal savings system, Japan's largest deposit-taking institution and a major supplier of funds to the FILP.
The FILP, dubbed Japan's second national budget, uses deposits from the MPT and the Welfare Ministry to fund government-affiliated financial institutions and other quasi-governmental bodies.

Analysts and some politicians have criticised the FILP for its massive size relative to the national budget, the large deficits of the quasi-governmental bodies it funds, and the low returns on its deposits.
The Welfare Ministry has said that deposits it receives from pension funds and places with FILP should be invested more efficiently.
